label: Bible Study
prompt: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of _____: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.
verse: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.
note: The motto of the whole book of Proverbs — wisdom's first lesson is reverence.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: For thus saith the LORD of hosts; After the glory hath he sent me unto the nations which spoiled you: for he that toucheth you toucheth the _____ of his eye.
verse: For thus saith the LORD of hosts; After the glory hath he sent me unto the nations which spoiled you: for he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye.
note: The 'apple' of the eye is the pupil — the part you guard by reflex. That's how God guards His people.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And there sat in a window a certain young man named Eutychus, being fallen into a deep sleep: and as Paul was long preaching, he sunk down with sleep, and fell down from the third _____, and was taken up dead.
verse: And there sat in a window a certain young man named Eutychus, being fallen into a deep sleep: and as Paul was long preaching, he sunk down with sleep, and fell down from the third loft, and was taken up dead.
note: Eutychus dozed off during Paul's long sermon and fell from the third loft — Paul revived him, then kept talking till dawn.

label: Deep Water
prompt: But my servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him, and hath followed me _____, him will I bring into the land whereinto he went; and his seed shall possess it.
verse: But my servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him, and hath followed me fully, him will I bring into the land whereinto he went; and his seed shall possess it.
note: Of twelve spies only Caleb and Joshua said 'we can' — Caleb finally claimed Hebron at eighty-five.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the _____.
verse: Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful.
note: The Psalter opens with a slow slide — walk, stand, sit — that ends in 'the seat of the scornful.'
